h1: Akyra Manor Chiang Mai — A Rooftop-Pool Boutique in the Heart of Nimman (Now AMANOR Hotel)
intro: Picture this: a dark-toned design room with a bathtub set out on your private balcony, soaking in warm water while you watch the city, then heading up to sip a cocktail by the rooftop infinity pool as the sun drops behind Doi Suthep — Akyra Manor Chiang Mai packs the feel of an urban hotel and a resort into one building in the middle of Nimman · A member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World, it opened in 2015 and rebranded as AMANOR Hotel in April 2025 · From approx. THB 3,900/night.

body.html: The overview and who it suits — Akyra Manor Chiang Mai first opened in 2015 under the Manor Group and has been a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World from the start · First, an important detail many travellers miss: on 1 April 2025 the hotel rebranded as AMANOR Hotel Chiang Mai after a decade of operation, still owned by Manor Group but now managed by Unicorn Hospitality · So if you search for "Akyra Manor" and see "AMANOR" on some platforms, don't be confused — it's the same place, same building, same location, same concept · What sets it apart from the usual Nimman hotel is its bold, dark-toned design and its positioning as a small boutique in the busiest district of Chiang Mai · Pulling together real guest reviews from Tripadvisor, Trip.com, Booking and Agoda, it suits couples, honeymooners, people marking a special occasion, and design-minded travellers who want a stylish boutique in a walkable area · On the other hand, if you're travelling with young kids and want a kids' club and children's activities, or you want sprawling resort gardens out of town, this may not be the best fit for you.

Location and getting around — Akyra Manor / AMANOR sits at 22/2 Nimmanhaemin Road, Soi 9, Suthep sub-district, Mueang Chiang Mai · The beauty of the location is that it tucks itself into Soi 9, so it's quieter than you'd expect, yet step out the door and you're in the thick of Nimman · A few minutes' walk gets you to the famous cafes, restaurants, gift shops, bars and roasters that made Nimman Chiang Mai's trendiest neighbourhood · It's about a 5-minute walk to MAYA Lifestyle Shopping Center, and roughly 7 minutes to One Nimman (an events plaza and handmade-goods market) · For the Old City, Tha Phae Gate and the temples inside the moat, it's about a 10-minute drive · The Night Bazaar is around 15 minutes · And very conveniently, it's only about 6 km from Chiang Mai International Airport (CNX), a 15-minute drive, which makes it ideal for short trips where you don't want to waste time in transit · One location note: because it's a building in a soi, parking is limited, so let the hotel know in advance if you're driving, and the charm of a central location comes with some street noise on certain nights, which we cover below.

Room types and design — The hotel has 62 rooms across an 8-floor building, in three main categories · Deluxe Room starts at around 30 sqm, ideal for couples who prioritise location and design on an accessible budget · Premier Suite at around 60 sqm adds a sitting area and a wider balcony · and the top Manor Suite at around 100 sqm has a separate living room and the most privacy, perfect for special-occasion trips or those who plan to spend most of their time in the room · The signature feature everyone talks about is the outdoor bathtub set on a private balcony in many room types, giving that bathe-in-the-city onsen feeling, and some upper categories even add an outdoor hot tub · Interiors use dark wood, glass and metal for an urban, masculine look, with Egyptian-linen bedding, large windows, and walk-in closets plus soaking tubs in select suites · There's a coffee machine, minibar, Smart TV, sound system and a pillow menu that guests love · An honest note from the reviews: the design leans dark and dim, so anyone who prefers a bright, airy room may find it on the gloomy side, and some lower-floor rooms have less open views, so flag light and view preferences when you book · A few post-rebrand reviews also note that some furniture and in-room fittings show wear consistent with a ten-year-old building, which is worth knowing in advance.

"Soaking in the balcony bathtub at night with a cool breeze, the noise of Nimman somewhere far below, then heading up to the rooftop pool to watch the city lights — this is a hotel that makes you not want to go anywhere."

Facilities, pool and spa — The highlight every review agrees on is the rooftop · The glass-edged infinity pool on the top floor looks out over the city skyline with the silhouette of Doi Suthep behind it, and many call it one of the best-atmosphere rooftop pools in the Nimman area · It isn't a long lap pool — it's more about relaxed swimming and photos than exercise · Beside the pool is the ARISE Rooftop Bar (formerly RISE Bar), serving bartender-crafted cocktails and drawing both hotel guests and locals in the evening · Happy hour is the best-value time and when the sunset view is at its finest · Beyond the rooftop there's a fitness room with equipment, spa and massage services for unwinding, and complimentary bicycles for exploring the Nimman area · Overall the facility list isn't as long as a big resort's — there's no water park or kids' club — but everything on offer is intentionally designed to fit the urban-boutique concept, and the rooftop is the single biggest reason people choose to stay here.

Food and bar — The main restaurant is lumi, serving modern Italian cuisine alongside classic Thai dishes, cooked by the hotel's chef with a focus on local and sustainable ingredients, and featuring a wood-fired pizza oven and an open show kitchen to watch while you wait · This is also where breakfast is served, and reviews speak well of it for both quality and freshness · For an evening drink you head up to ARISE on the rooftop, which has become the property's signature for atmosphere · One honest note: food and drink prices inside the hotel sit at luxury-hotel level, higher than the restaurants in Nimman just a few steps away · The upside is that if you want to save, you can simply walk out to Nimman's famous eateries without taking a car — a real advantage of the central location compared with out-of-town luxury resorts where you're tied to the in-house restaurant.

Service — The thing Akyra Manor / AMANOR is praised for most consistently in reviews is its staff · Thanks to its modest size and high staff-to-guest ratio, the care here is genuinely close and personal · Many guests describe staff remembering their names, recalling their drink and food preferences, and offering small welcome touches or upgrades without being asked · The team speaks multiple languages including English and Chinese, and helps arrange transport, restaurant bookings and local recommendations · The overall feel is grown-up, leaning into quiet and privacy rather than being a family hotel full of running children · This is a big reason guests return and keep scoring service highly — and notably, even in post-rebrand reviews where some worried standards might slip, most confirm the service is still as good as before.

What real guests say (praise and gripes) — Pulling from multiple platforms, the most consistent praise goes to the distinctive room design, the outdoor balcony bathtubs, the rooftop with its infinity pool and ARISE Bar, the walkable central-Nimman location, and the attentive service · The gripes are few and fairly clear: first, night-time noise from the neighbourhood — street-facing rooms can hear the bars and traffic on Friday and Saturday nights, so light sleepers should request an inner or higher room · second, dark, dim rooms and some less open views, not to everyone's taste · third, high in-house food and drink prices · and fourth, a few post-rebrand reviews noting wear on some furniture consistent with the building's age · Overall the scores remain very high: on Tripadvisor it holds around 4.9/5 from over 2,000 reviews and ranks roughly #4 of 540 hotels in Chiang Mai · On Trip.com and Booking it sits in the low-9s, which shows most guests come away impressed.

Price comparison and value — Starting rates run from around THB 3,900–5,000/night for a Deluxe Room in good-price windows, climbing to roughly THB 6,500 for a Premier Suite and THB 9,000+ for a Manor Suite in high season · Compared with other 5-star luxury hotels in Chiang Mai, this place wins clearly on price-to-location ratio — you get Small Luxury Hotels of the World design, a rooftop pool and an outdoor bathtub at a price far more accessible than riverside or out-of-town luxury properties · Next to 137 Pillars House (from ~THB 18,000) or Raya Heritage (from ~THB 9,800), both outside the tourist core, Akyra Manor is easier on both price and location · Four Seasons in Mae Rim is in a different price bracket entirely · The trade-off to weigh: if you want big gardens, large resort grounds and out-of-town silence, the riverside hotels deliver more — but if you value walkability and urban design, this is excellent value at its price · It's also worth remembering what you save indirectly: with cafes, restaurants and shopping all within a short walk, you're far less reliant on taxis and Grab than you would be at an out-of-town resort, and those small daily savings add up over a multi-night stay.

What to know before you book — One, know that the official name is now AMANOR Hotel Chiang Mai, but many platforms still list the old Akyra Manor name — it's the same hotel · Two, if you're a light sleeper, request an inner or higher room not facing the street at booking, especially for Friday/Saturday nights · Three, if you want full use of the outdoor bathtub, confirm with the hotel that your room has a balcony tub and a genuinely private balcony, as not all rooms are identical after the rebrand · Four, if light and views matter, ask for a higher floor · Five, check whether your package includes breakfast, since lumi's freshly cooked breakfast is good value when bundled · Six, parking is limited as it's a building in a soi, so notify the hotel if you're driving · Seven, in high season (November–February, Chiang Mai's peak travel months) rooms fill fast, so book ahead, lock a free-cancellation rate, and compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.

The verdict — Akyra Manor Chiang Mai (today's AMANOR Hotel) is the boutique for people who want sharp design, a rooftop pool, an outdoor bathtub, and a central-Nimman location you can walk out of and start exploring immediately — at a price more accessible than riverside or out-of-town luxury hotels · It suits couples, special-occasion trips and design-minded travellers who want both city energy and a place to retreat in one building · What you accept: a central location brings some night noise on certain nights, the rooms lean dark and aren't for everyone, and it's a ten-year-old building with some wear · But with review scores that remain high even after the rebrand, Small Luxury Hotels of the World membership, and a location that's hard to find in the Nimman area, Akyra Manor / AMANOR remains one of Chiang Mai's best-value 5-star boutiques for the right traveller · For a first-time visitor who wants to be where the action is, soak in a balcony tub at night and toast the mountains from a rooftop pool, it's an easy hotel to recommend.

faqTitle: FAQ — Akyra Manor Chiang Mai (AMANOR Hotel)

faq.q: Are Akyra Manor and AMANOR Hotel Chiang Mai the same place?
faq.a: Yes · they're the same hotel · It opened in 2015 as Akyra Manor Chiang Mai and rebranded as AMANOR Hotel Chiang Mai on 1 April 2025 after a decade, still owned by Manor Group, now managed by Unicorn Hospitality · Some platforms still list the old Akyra Manor name — same building, same location.

faq.q: Where is Akyra Manor / AMANOR and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 22/2 Nimmanhaemin Road, Soi 9, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, in the heart of Nimman · A few minutes' walk to famous cafes and restaurants · About 5 minutes to MAYA and 7 minutes to One Nimman · Around 10 minutes by car to the Old City, and only about 6 km (15 minutes) from Chiang Mai Airport.

faq.q: What's the starting price and what room types are there?
faq.a: From around THB 3,900/night for a Deluxe Room (~30 sqm) · Larger options are the Premier Suite (~60 sqm) and Manor Suite (~100 sqm) · Many rooms have an outdoor balcony bathtub · High-season rates rise, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Akyra Manor best for?
faq.a: Best for couples, special-occasion trips and design-minded travellers who want a stylish boutique in a walkable area · The vibe is grown-up and quiet rather than a family hotel for young kids · Ideal for people who want to be in the heart of Nimman with a rooftop pool and design rooms to return to.

faq.q: Does it have a rooftop pool and bar?
faq.a: Yes · a glass-edged rooftop infinity pool with views over the city and Doi Suthep · paired with ARISE Rooftop Bar (formerly RISE Bar) and an evening happy hour · Many reviews call it the highlight of the hotel.

faq.q: Is it noisy, and which room should I request?
faq.a: Being in the heart of Nimman, street-facing rooms can hear the neighbourhood at night on Friday/Saturday · Light sleepers should request an inner or higher room at booking · Most rooms are quiet, but flagging your preference in advance helps a lot.
